facts.claim: Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum
facts.context: The eruption is traditionally dated to August AD 79, though an inscription found in 2018 points to October.
facts.goDeeper: The date is still argued over; autumn fruit and heavy clothing found on site support the later date.

source.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

facts.claim: Systematic excavation of Pompeii began
facts.context: Digging began in 1748 under the King of Naples, after Herculaneum was found a decade earlier.
facts.goDeeper: Early work was closer to treasure hunting than archaeology; tunnels were dug and frescoes cut from walls.

facts.claim: Estimated deaths in the eruption of Vesuvius
facts.context: Around 2,000 bodies have been found at Pompeii, though the true toll across the region was likely higher.
facts.goDeeper: Many residents had fled during the earlier stages; those who stayed were killed by the surges of hot gas.

source.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

facts.claim: Estimated population of Pompeii before the eruption
facts.context: Estimates run from about 11,000 to 15,000 for the town at its height.
facts.goDeeper: It was a prosperous provincial port, not a great city — which is partly why the ordinary detail survives.

facts.claim: Depth of ash and pumice that buried Pompeii
facts.context: Roughly four to six metres of volcanic debris covered the town.
facts.goDeeper: Herculaneum was buried far deeper, under about 20 metres of hot mud and ash, which preserved wood and even food.

facts.claim: Height of the eruption column above Vesuvius
facts.context: The column reached roughly 33 km into the stratosphere at its peak.
facts.goDeeper: Pliny the Younger described it as shaped like an umbrella pine. Eruptions of this type are now called Plinian.

source.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

facts.claim: A severe earthquake damaged Pompeii years before the eruption
facts.context: A major quake struck in AD 62; parts of the town were still being rebuilt in 79.
facts.goDeeper: Nobody connected the tremors with the mountain. Vesuvius was not recognised as a volcano at all.

facts.claim: Giuseppe Fiorelli devised the technique of casting the voids left by bodies
facts.context: Fiorelli poured plaster into cavities in the ash, reproducing the shape of people at the moment of death.
facts.goDeeper: The bodies had decayed away, leaving perfect moulds. Some casts capture clothing and facial expressions.

facts.claim: Area of the excavated site at Pompeii
facts.context: About 44 hectares of the roughly 66-hectare town have been uncovered.
facts.goDeeper: A third is deliberately left buried, on the view that future archaeologists will have better methods.

facts.claim: Present height of Mount Vesuvius
facts.context: About 1,281 metres today. The 79 eruption removed a large part of the original summit.
facts.goDeeper: Around three million people now live close enough to be at risk, making it one of the most dangerous volcanoes on earth.

facts.claim: Vesuvius last erupted
facts.context: The most recent eruption was in March 1944, during the Allied campaign in Italy.
facts.goDeeper: It destroyed dozens of American B-25 bombers parked at a nearby airfield.

facts.claim: Age of Pliny the Younger when he witnessed the eruption
facts.context: He was about 17, watching from across the bay at Misenum, and wrote his account decades later.
facts.goDeeper: His uncle Pliny the Elder sailed towards the eruption to help evacuate people and died in the attempt.

facts.claim: Carbonised loaves of bread have been recovered from Pompeii and Herculaneum
facts.context: Bread was found still in the ovens, carbonised but intact, some stamped with the baker's mark.
facts.goDeeper: One bakery's loaf was scored into eight segments, the same way focaccia is divided in Naples today.

facts.claim: Thousands of pieces of graffiti survive on Pompeii's walls
facts.context: More than 11,000 inscriptions have been recorded: election slogans, insults, prices, love notes and jokes.
facts.goDeeper: One reads: 'I am amazed, wall, that you have not collapsed under the weight of so much writing.'

facts.claim: Pompeii was destroyed by flowing lava
facts.context: There was no lava flow. The town was buried by falling pumice and then struck by pyroclastic surges of scorching gas and ash.
facts.goDeeper: The surges moved at over 100 km per hour and were hot enough to kill instantly.

source.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

facts.claim: Pliny the Elder died during the eruption
facts.context: He crossed the bay by ship to observe the eruption and rescue survivors, and died on the shore at Stabiae.
facts.goDeeper: He was the author of the Natural History, a 37-volume encyclopedia of everything then known.

facts.claim: A library of scrolls survived carbonised at Herculaneum
facts.context: Around 1,800 scrolls were found in the Villa of the Papyri, charred solid by the heat.
facts.goDeeper: They are now being read without unrolling them, using X-ray scanning and machine learning.

facts.claim: The location of Pompeii was completely forgotten for centuries
facts.context: The site was lost for about 1,500 years, though the local name Civita hinted that something lay beneath.
facts.goDeeper: It was rediscovered by workmen digging a water channel.

facts.claim: Pompeii had street counters serving hot food to passers-by
facts.context: Around 80 thermopolia have been identified, with sunken jars in a masonry counter for serving hot dishes.
facts.goDeeper: One excavated in 2020 still had traces of duck, goat, fish and snails in its jars.

facts.claim: Pompeii is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
facts.context: Inscribed in 1997 along with Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata.
facts.goDeeper: It is among Italy's most visited sites, which is itself a preservation problem.
